Add/drop closes tomorrow at noon and I'm underwater this semester. I'm on an F-1 student visa and I'm enrolled in twelve credits, and twelve is the full-time minimum at my school. My four courses are a three-credit organic chemistry course, statistics, a writing seminar and a physics lab section.

Honestly, the semester has been chaotic. I took on a teaching assistant shift at the chemistry stockroom, which eats eleven hours a week, and my roommate moved out in September so I have been splitting the rent with a stranger from a listing site. My grandmother has also been in and out of hospital back home, so my evenings are often spent on the phone with my aunt. Organic chemistry has the heaviest workload by far: a problem set every Thursday, a quiz every other Monday, and a lab report that the professor grades as if it were a journal submission. I did well on the first midterm, but the second one covered reaction mechanisms I had barely seen in lecture because the professor was away at a conference that week. Statistics is going fine, the writing seminar is mostly reading and a short response paper each week, and the lab section is a single afternoon. I have been sleeping about five hours a night, my skin has broken out, and I keep forgetting to eat lunch. My adviser is hard to catch because she teaches on Tuesdays and Thursdays and her office hours fill up weeks ahead.

I just want the quickest way to lighten my load before the deadline.

A) Ask the international student office before changing my schedule
B) Drop organic chemistry through the student portal tonight
C) Stay in all four courses and push through the semester

B) Wait and submit the application after I am back from Portugal

At weekends we walk along the canal and stop at a cafe with a ramp for the pram, then take turns napping in the afternoon.

Should I just skip the claim?

A) Ask Citizens Advice before deciding
B) Claim and take the payments, with my partner repaying the extra through self assessment
C) Skip the Child Benefit claim altogether
